subject: Vectorized Bernoulli distribution to draw many variables

messages.author: 8df77a1c1b1da14e
messages.subject: Vectorized Bernoulli distribution to draw many variables
parts:
I have a situation where I need to draw many Bernoulli variable, and it is time-consuming.

In this post (https://groups.google.com/g/nimble-users/c/8vaTHQoJz2M/m/kPKsOpMZAgAJ), Perry suggests a vectorized Bernoulli distribution as one strategy to reduce computation time (although in that example it was not to simulate values). I tried to use this approach, but when I register dVectorBernoulli as a discrete distribution, and then replace the RW block sampler with a binary sampler:

confMCMC$removeSamplers(c("z"))
confMCMC$addSampler(target = "z", type = "binary")
nimMCMC <- buildMCMC(confMCMC)

it produces the following error:


Error in samplerFunction(model = model, mvSaved = mvSaved, target = target, :
cannot use binary sampler on more than one target node

Perhaps it will not save as much computation time as I hope, but can I accomplish this action of drawing a vector of Bernoulli variables without a loop? Also, is it necessary to provide the random generating function?

Below is a simple contrived example that reproduces the error.  

Thanks,
Glenn

#######################################################
library(nimble)

# generate occupancy data
nsites <- 50
nocc <- 5
b0 <- 0.5
b1 <- 0.25
x <- rnorm(nsites)
psi <- plogis(b0 + b1 * x)
z <- rbinom(nsites, 1, psi)
p <- 0.3
y <- rbinom(nsites, nocc, z*p)

# Vectorized Bernoulli distribution
dBernoulliVector <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(x    = double(1),
                 prob = double(1),
                 log  = integer(0, default = 0)) { ## default should be zero
    returnType(double(0))
    logProb <- sum(dbinom(x, size = 1, prob = prob, log = TRUE))
    if(log) return(logProb) else return(exp(logProb))
  }
)
rBernoulliVector <- nimbleFunction( # is this necessary?
    run = function(n = integer(0), prob = double(1)) {
        returnType(double(1))
        x <- rbinom(n, 1, prob)
        return(x)
    })
nimble::registerDistributions(list(
    dBernoulliVector = list(
        BUGSdist = "dBernoulliVector(prob)",
        types = c(
            "value = double(1)",
    "prob = double(1)",
            "log = double(0)"
        ),
        discrete = TRUE
    )
))

# specify the occupancy model
modelcode <- nimbleCode({
     p ~ dbeta(1,1)
     for(i in 1:2){
  b[i] ~ dnorm(0,1)
     }
 
  logit(psi[1:nsites]) <- b[1] + b[2] * x[1:nsites]
  z[1:nsites] ~ dBernoulliVector(psi[1:nsites])
  for(i in 1:nsites){
  y[i] ~ dbinom(size = nocc, prob = p * z[i])
   }
})

init <- list(p = 0.25, b = runif(2), z = as.numeric(y>0))
parameters <- c("p", "b")

ni  <- 10
nb <- .2
bin <- ni * nb
nt <- 1
nc <- 3

Rmodel <- nimbleModel(code = modelcode,
                         name = "modelcode",
                         data = list(y = y, x = x),
                         constants = list(nsites = nsites, nocc = nocc),
                          inits = init)
Cnim <- compileNimble(Rmodel,  showCompilerOutput = FALSE)
confMCMC <- configureMCMC(Rmodel,
                            monitors = parameters,
                            thin = nt,
                            useConjugacy = FALSE)
confMCMC$removeSamplers(c("z"))
confMCMC$addSampler(target = "z", type = "binary")
confMCMC$printSamplers('z')

nimMCMC <- buildMCMC(confMCMC)                # generates the error
CnimMCMC <- compileNimble(nimMCMC,
                            project = Rmodel, showCompilerOutput = FALSE)

CnimMCMC$run(niter = 1)
results <- runMCMC(CnimMCMC,
                  niter = ni,
                  nburnin = bin,
                  nchains = nc
                  )

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Vectorized Bernoulli distribution to draw many variables
parts:
Hi Glenn,

I think the issue here is that now "z[1:nsites]" is a single vector node, but the "binary" sampler only handles scalar nodes. You could include "targetByNode = TRUE" and "multivariateNodesAsScalars = TRUE" in "addSampler" to make it treat each element of z as a scalar node for sampling and then to expand the target "z" into all of those scalar elements with a separate sampler for each. But this is the same sampling scheme you would get if you create each "z[i]" as an actual scalar node. And with the vector version, the log probability calculation for any scalar z[i] will include calculation of the entire vector, which isn't really necessary. So I'm not sure this looks helpful for your case. 

HTH
Perry

messages.author: 8df77a1c1b1da14e
messages.subject: Re: Vectorized Bernoulli distribution to draw many variables
parts:
Thanks Perry, that's helpful.

I tried a creative workaround where I instead created a dUniformVector function that can be sampled with a RW Block sampler, followed by a step function to  convert the vector of uniform variables to the desired 0/1 z[1:nsites] vector.
logit(psi[1:nsites]) <- b[1] + b[2] * x[1:nsites]

z_unif[1:nsites] ~ dUniformVector(0,1)
z[1:nsites] <- step(psi[1:nsites] - z_unif[1:nsites])

In preliminary testing there was no gain at all in speed over the case where I loop over Bernoulli draws for each z[i], and in fact it was slightly slower.  Maybe that's because of the need to do the additional (inefficient?) step function. Moreover, mixing/convergence was very bad, which in retrospect I probably should have expected.

Perhaps the best bet is to rewrite the model to eliminate the need to estimate all those latent states.

messages.author: 8df77a1c1b1da14e
messages.subject: Re: Vectorized Bernoulli distribution to draw many variables
parts:
I have another question related to vectorizing gneration of random variable, this dime with dcat.
Looping over many calls to dcat seems pretty inefficient, so I wanted to try a vectorized function to see if I could gain any speed. But I can't get it to work.

The function looks like:

# for a vector of categorical variables
dCatVector <- nimbleFunction(

run = function(x    = double(1),
                 prob = double(1),
                 log  = integer(0, default = 0)) { ## default should be zero
    returnType(double(0))
logProb <- sum(dcat(x, prob = prob, log = TRUE))

if(log) return(logProb) else return(exp(logProb))
  }
)
rCatVector <- nimbleFunction(

run = function(n = integer(0), prob = double(1)) {
        returnType(double(1))

x <- rcat(n, prob)
        return(x)
    })

nimble::registerDistributions(list(
    dCatVector = list(
        BUGSdist = "dCatVector(prob)",

types = c(
            "value = double(1)",
"prob = double(1)",
            "log = double(0)"
        ),
        discrete = TRUE
    )
))

This seems to work when I build and calculate the model, but it fails when I try to compile the model, with the following messages:

Warning: we currently expect to see a 1 and only a 1 as the first argument to an rcat or rinterval call
Error: Number of dimensions 0 of the return() argument does not match number 1 given in the returnType() statement.
 This occurred for: return(x)
 This was part of the call:  {
  x <- nimArr_rcat(prob=ARG2_prob_)
  return(x)

This puzzling to me because the rcat function does accept an n>1 argument. Is it just compiled that rcat no longer accepts an n>1 argument? If that is the case, then is it not possible to do what I want to do?
The rmulti function also expects n=1 as the first agrument, and the R function rmultinom is apparently not supported.

messages.author: d78486bfff620d81
messages.subject: Re: Vectorized Bernoulli distribution to draw many variables
parts:
hi Glenn,

That's correct that in compiled execution we can't handle n>1 (related to the fact that C++ is statically typed). To achieve what you want, just put `rcat` in a loop in `rCatVector`. That loop will be run in C++ so there's no efficiency problem in having a loop there. 

-Chris

messages.author: 8df77a1c1b1da14e
messages.subject: Re: Vectorized Bernoulli distribution to draw many variables
parts:
Thanks Chris,

I tried what you suggested, but ran into the problem that the default assigned RW_block sampler is not allowed for discrete variable, and the categorical sampler produces the error ' cannot use categorical sampler on more than one target node' . I tried to instead assign an AF_slice sampler. All seemed well until the 'runMCMC' step upon which R crashed. Could this be because of bad default control parameter? I'm a bit out of my depth here. I also tried the  "targetByNode = TRUE" and "multivariateNodesAsScalars = TRUE" approach for the categorical sampler that Perry suggested above for a vectorized Bernoulli, and that also crashed R.

I tried one other thing, and that is to draw a multinomial of size = 'length of desired latent categorical vector', and then use the R function sample (via nimbleRcall) to randomly assign the resulting multinomial classes into the desired categorical vector. This seemed to work and was MUCH faster than looping through calls to dcat in the model code. But I don't trust the results, because I don't think it is appropriately updating the specific latent variables. Without going into too much detail, I think it might be because, although the prior probabilities are the same for each latent variable in the vector, the hazard for each categorical class changes depending on when the event occurs, and this multinomial approach does not track the estimated hazard of events corresponding to specific latent variables in the multinomial step. Instead it only track the total number of events that end up in each class. In any case, the results do not agree with those from the simpler, but inefficient approach of looping through calls to dcat.

Again, I think the best way forward might be to marginalize out the latent variables. But it sure would be nice at some point to figure out how to efficiently draw many categorical (or Bernoulli) variables. I'll report back here if I ever figure out an efficient vectorized solution. Maybe C++ constraints mean it simply is not possible.

parts:
Hmm, an R crash should not be happening.

Are you able to share a minimal reproducible example for us to look at (either on- or off-list, as you prefer)? 

-chris
On Mon, Aug 24, 2026 at 2:06 PM gesta...@gmail.com <gesta...@gmail.com> wrote:

Thanks Chris,

I tried what you suggested, but ran into the problem that the default assigned RW_block sampler is not allowed for discrete variable, and the categorical sampler produces the error ' cannot use categorical sampler on more than one target node' . I tried to instead assign an AF_slice sampler. All seemed well until the 'runMCMC' step upon which R crashed. Could this be because of bad default control parameter? I'm a bit out of my depth here. I also tried the  "targetByNode = TRUE" and "multivariateNodesAsScalars = TRUE" approach for the categorical sampler that Perry suggested above for a vectorized Bernoulli, and that also crashed R.

I tried one other thing, and that is to draw a multinomial of size = 'length of desired latent categorical vector', and then use the R function sample (via nimbleRcall) to randomly assign the resulting multinomial classes into the desired categorical vector. This seemed to work and was MUCH faster than looping through calls to dcat in the model code. But I don't trust the results, because I don't think it is appropriately updating the specific latent variables. Without going into too much detail, I think it might be because, although the prior probabilities are the same for each latent variable in the vector, the hazard for each categorical class changes depending on when the event occurs, and this multinomial approach does not track the estimated hazard of events corresponding to specific latent variables in the multinomial step. Instead it only track the total number of events that end up in each class. In any case, the results do not agree with those from the simpler, but inefficient approach of looping through calls to dcat.

Again, I think the best way forward might be to marginalize out the latent variables. But it sure would be nice at some point to figure out how to efficiently draw many categorical (or Bernoulli) variables. I'll report back here if I ever figure out an efficient vectorized solution. Maybe C++ constraints mean it simply is not possible.


On Friday, August 21, 2026 at 5:00:22 PM UTC-5 Chris Paciorek wrote:
hi Glenn,

That's correct that in compiled execution we can't handle n>1 (related to the fact that C++ is statically typed). To achieve what you want, just put `rcat` in a loop in `rCatVector`. That loop will be run in C++ so there's no efficiency problem in having a loop there. 

-Chris

On Tue, Aug 18, 2026 at 10:16 AM gesta...@gmail.com <gesta...@gmail.com> wrote:
I have another question related to vectorizing gneration of random variable, this dime with dcat.
Looping over many calls to dcat seems pretty inefficient, so I wanted to try a vectorized function to see if I could gain any speed. But I can't get it to work.

The function looks like:

# for a vector of categorical variables
dCatVector <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(x    = double(1),
                 prob = double(1),
                 log  = integer(0, default = 0)) { ## default should be zero
    returnType(double(0))
    logProb <- sum(dcat(x, prob = prob, log = TRUE))
    if(log) return(logProb) else return(exp(logProb))
  }
)
rCatVector <- nimbleFunction(
    run = function(n = integer(0), prob = double(1)) {
        returnType(double(1))
        x <- rcat(n, prob)
        return(x)
    })

nimble::registerDistributions(list(
    dCatVector = list(
        BUGSdist = "dCatVector(prob)",
        types = c(
            "value = double(1)",
"prob = double(1)",
            "log = double(0)"
        ),
        discrete = TRUE
    )
))

This seems to work when I build and calculate the model, but it fails when I try to compile the model, with the following messages:

Warning: we currently expect to see a 1 and only a 1 as the first argument to an rcat or rinterval call
Error: Number of dimensions 0 of the return() argument does not match number 1 given in the returnType() statement.
 This occurred for: return(x)
 This was part of the call:  {
  x <- nimArr_rcat(prob=ARG2_prob_)
  return(x)

This puzzling to me because the rcat function does accept an n>1 argument. Is it just compiled that rcat no longer accepts an n>1 argument? If that is the case, then is it not possible to do what I want to do?
The rmulti function also expects n=1 as the first agrument, and the R function rmultinom is apparently not supported.
